newsitem.title: CANADA: Chile may cut barley, durum tariffs on Canada-CWB.
newsitem.headline: Chile may cut barley, durum tariffs on Canada-CWB.

text.p: Canada could expand its share of Chile's grain market if Chile approves a plan to cut import tariffs on Canadian barley and durum, a Canadian Wheat Board market analyst said Tuesday.
"This was in the Canada-Chile free trade agreement earlier this year," said Maureen Bader, a Latin American market analyst for the Wheat Board.
"It puts us at a really good position against Australia where they typically buy almost all of their barley," Bader said.
Chile's lower Chamber of Deputies approved the treaty May 20 by a vote of 78 to 21 with 10 abstentions, but the pact may face a tougher vote in the Senate this month.
Chile charges an 11 percent import tariff on grains from all origins, the CWB said.

"I don't know if we'll be able to capture the entire 11 percent price differential because they don't typically import barley from us," Bader said. "We may over time be able to do that once they get used to the varieties we produce here."
Canada exported 100,000 tonnes of durum and 5,000 tonnes of barley to Chile in the 1995/96 (August/July) crop year, according to the CWB's 1995/96 annual report.
